baslik: One Cracked Wheel Rim Derailed a High-Speed Train
sonuc: derailed and crashed into a bridge
tetik: a fatigue crack in a steel wheel tyre
mekanizma: fatigue fracture of a rubber-cushioned wheel's outer tyre, which then struck the points
ders: resilient wheels were replaced with solid monobloc wheels on German high-speed trains
yanilgi: The wheel design came from trams, which run at much lower speed. It had not been tested for high-speed fatigue.
tartisma: A passenger reported noise and vibration before the crash. When should a train stop on a passenger's word?
basliklar: Why the Eschede Train Crashed
The Wheel Design Borrowed From Trams
sahneler: A German high-speed train derailed and slammed into a road bridge.
The bridge collapsed onto the carriages, and one hundred one people were killed.
It began with a single wheel.
The wheels had a steel tyre cushioned by rubber.
That design came from trams, not high-speed trains.
A fatigue crack grew until the tyre broke free.
It jammed into the points and derailed the train.
German high-speed trains switched to solid steel wheels.

baslik: The Unattended Oil Train That Rolled Into a Town
sonuc: rolled into town, derailed and exploded
tetik: too few handbrakes on an unattended train on a slope
mekanizma: air brakes releasing after the locomotive was shut down, with insufficient handbrakes to hold the train
ders: Canada tightened rules on securing trains and on tank car design
yanilgi: Nobody was driving it. The train was parked for the night and began rolling on its own.
tartisma: Firefighters shut down the burning locomotive, which disabled its air brakes. Who could have known?
basliklar: Why the Lac-Mégantic Train Rolled Into Town
The Runaway Train With Nobody Aboard
sahneler: In the middle of the night, a runaway oil train rolled into a Quebec town.
It derailed and exploded, and forty seven people were killed.
Nobody was aboard.
It had been parked uphill with too few handbrakes applied.
A fire broke out on the locomotive.
When the engine was shut down, its air brakes slowly released.
The train began rolling down toward the town.
Canada tightened rules for securing trains and building tank cars.

baslik: A Driver Trying to Make Up 90 Seconds Took a Curve Too Fast
tetik: a driver speeding to recover a small delay
mekanizma: overspeed on a curve without automatic speed enforcement
ders: JR West installed modern automatic train stop systems on curves
yanilgi: The delay was tiny. Harsh punishment for lateness pushed drivers to take risks to recover seconds.
tartisma: Drivers faced humiliating retraining for small delays. Can company culture cause a derailment?
basliklar: Why the Amagasaki Train Derailed
The Culture That Punished Delays
sahneler: A packed commuter train derailed on a curve near Osaka.
It slammed into an apartment building, and one hundred seven people died.
The driver was running slightly late.
Drivers faced harsh punishment for even small delays.
He entered the curve far above the speed limit.
No automatic system forced the train to slow down.
The front carriages left the track.
JR West then installed modern speed enforcement on curves.

baslik: A Lightning Strike Turned a Red Signal Green
mekanizma: signal equipment fault after a lightning strike showing a clear line despite a stopped train
ders: China reviewed its signalling systems and slowed high-speed services
yanilgi: The system didn't fail safe. After the lightning strike, it showed clear track where a train was standing.
tartisma: The wreckage was buried quickly at the site. Should evidence be preserved no matter what?
basliklar: Why the Wenzhou Trains Collided
The Signal That Showed Green by Mistake
sahneler: Two high-speed trains collided on a viaduct near Wenzhou.
Carriages fell from the viaduct, and forty people were killed.
Lightning had struck the signalling equipment.
A train stalled on the track ahead.
The damaged system reported that section as clear.
A second train was sent into it at speed.
The wreckage was hastily buried, drawing public anger.
China reviewed its signals and slowed its high-speed trains.

baslik: The Signalmen Forgot a Train Standing on the Line
tetik: a local train forgotten on the main line during a shift change
mekanizma: signalling error during an irregular shift handover, followed by a multiple collision and fire
ders: track-occupation reminders and later track circuits became standard
zincir: LOCAL TRAIN PARKED ON MAIN LINE
yanilgi: The signals worked. The signalmen forgot a train that was standing right outside their window.
tartisma: The shift change was informal and hidden from the logbook. Why do informal shortcuts spread?
basliklar: Why the Quintinshill Rail Disaster Happened
The Train Forgotten Outside the Window
sahneler: A troop train crashed into a stationary train at Quintinshill in Scotland.
An express then hit the wreckage, and fire killed more than two hundred people.
The local train was standing on the main line.
It was right outside the signal box window.
The signalmen were changing shifts late and informally.
They forgot the train was there.
Britain's worst rail disaster followed.
Reminders for occupied lines, and later track circuits, became standard.

baslik: An Express in Fog Ran Past Its Signals
sonuc: caused a triple collision in a station
tetik: an express passing danger signals in fog
mekanizma: signals passed at danger in poor visibility, with no automatic warning system
ders: Britain accelerated fitting the Automatic Warning System
zincir: EXPRESS PASSES CAUTION AND DANGER SIGNALS
yanilgi: The signals were correctly set. In fog, with no in-cab warning, the driver passed them.
tartisma: An automatic warning system was already being trialled. Why do proven fixes take so long to roll out?
basliklar: Why the Harrow and Wealdstone Crash Happened
The Express That Missed Its Signals in Fog
soru: Why do fixes take so long?
sahneler: An express train ran into a crowded commuter train at Harrow station.
A second express then crashed into the wreckage, and one hundred twelve people died.
There was thick fog that morning.
The express passed its warning and danger signals.
Nothing in the cab alerted the driver.
An automatic warning system was already being tested.
It was not yet fitted on that line.
Britain then accelerated fitting it across the network.

baslik: A Volcanic Mudflow Took Out a Bridge Minutes Before a Train
tetik: a lahar from a volcano's crater lake
mekanizma: lahar undermining and destroying a bridge pier moments before the train crossed
ders: New Zealand installed a lahar warning system on the river
yanilgi: The bridge had no structural defect. A volcanic mudflow struck it minutes before the train arrived.
tartisma: A passer-by tried to warn the train with a torch. How do you warn a train in minutes?
basliklar: Why the Tangiwai Bridge Collapsed
The Volcanic Mudflow Minutes Before the Train
soru: How do you warn a train in minutes?
sahneler: On Christmas Eve, a train plunged off a bridge in New Zealand.
Carriages fell into a raging river, and one hundred fifty one people were killed.
Minutes earlier, a volcanic mudflow had struck the bridge.
The crater lake on Mount Ruapehu had broken out.
The lahar raced down the river and damaged a pier.
A passer-by tried to warn the train with a torch.
It was too late.
A lahar warning system now watches the river.

baslik: The Train That Crashed Through a Station Wall
sonuc: burst through the station wall onto the street
tetik: an express arriving too fast with brakes that failed to stop it
mekanizma: overrun from excessive speed and ineffective braking at a terminus
ders: the photo became one of the most famous images of a rail accident
yanilgi: Almost everyone aboard survived. The one person killed was a woman on the street below.
tartisma: The driver was trying to make up lost time. How often does lateness lead to danger?
basliklar: Why a Train Crashed Through the Montparnasse Station Wall
The Famous Photo of a Train Hanging Over a Street
soru: How often does lateness cause danger?
sahneler: An express train crashed through the wall of a Paris station.
The locomotive plunged onto the street below.
It was running late and entered the station too fast.
Its brakes couldn't stop it in time.
It overran the buffer stop and burst through the wall.
Almost everyone aboard survived.
A woman on the street below was killed.
The photograph became one of history's most famous rail images.

baslik: The Track Circuit That Couldn't See a Train
sonuc: collided when one train didn't detect another
tetik: a track circuit that stopped detecting trains
mekanizma: a faulty track circuit losing train detection, so automatic control sped the following train
ders: Metro replaced faulty circuits and added continuous monitoring
yanilgi: The following train wasn't driven carelessly. The automatic system believed the track ahead was empty.
tartisma: Similar circuit faults had appeared before. How do you monitor a system that fails silently?
basliklar: Why the Washington Metro Trains Collided
The Train the System Couldn't See
soru: How do you catch silent failures?
sahneler: Two Washington Metro trains collided during the evening rush.
One car was crushed, and nine people were killed.
The first train had stopped on the track.
A faulty track circuit failed to detect it.
To the automatic system, the track ahead looked empty.
It sent the following train on at speed.
The operator braked, but too late.
Metro replaced the circuits and added continuous monitoring.

baslik: An Amtrak Train Took a Curve at Twice the Limit
sonuc: derailed on a curve in Philadelphia
tetik: the train entering a curve at about twice the speed limit
mekanizma: overspeed on a curve, with positive train control not yet active on that section
ders: Positive Train Control was activated on the Northeast Corridor
yanilgi: The engineer wasn't on his phone. Investigators concluded he lost track of where he was.
tartisma: The speed-control system was installed nearby but not on that curve. Is partial protection enough?
basliklar: Why Amtrak Train 188 Derailed
The Curve Taken at Twice the Limit
sahneler: An Amtrak train derailed on a sharp curve in Philadelphia.
Carriages were torn apart, and eight people were killed.
The train entered the curve at about twice the speed limit.
The engineer had lost track of where he was.
He accelerated instead of slowing down.
Automatic speed control wasn't active on that curve.
Nothing stopped the train from overspeeding.
The system was activated on the Northeast Corridor soon after.

baslik: Why a Flagship Phone Was Banned From Planes
sonuc: had batteries overheat and catch fire
tetik: defects that let battery electrodes touch
mekanizma: internal short circuits from battery design and manufacturing defects in two different suppliers' cells
ders: Samsung introduced a multi-point battery safety check
yanilgi: The replacement phones weren't the fix. They had a different battery defect and also caught fire.
tartisma: The first recall was rushed. How fast should a company be sure of a fix?
basliklar: Why the Galaxy Note 7 Caught Fire
The Phone That Failed Its Recall
sahneler: A new flagship smartphone began catching fire.
Within weeks, airlines banned it from flights.
The problem was inside its battery.
In one design, the electrodes could be bent and touch.
That created a short circuit and runaway heating.
Replacement phones used a different battery.
They had their own defect and caught fire too.
The phone was discontinued, and battery testing was overhauled.

sonuc: caught fire, grounding the entire fleet
tetik: a cell short circuit spreading heat to neighbouring cells
mekanizma: thermal runaway in lithium-ion cells propagating through a battery without adequate containment
ders: the battery was redesigned with cell insulation and a steel containment box
yanilgi: The batteries didn't fail in flight first. The first fire broke out on a parked aircraft in Boston.
tartisma: Certification assumed cell failures wouldn't spread. How do you test for the case you think can't happen?
basliklar: Why Boeing 787 Batteries Caught Fire
The Battery Fires That Grounded a New Jet
sahneler: A battery caught fire on a parked Boeing 787 in Boston.
Within days, another overheated in flight, and every 787 was grounded.
The jets used large lithium-ion batteries.
One cell could short-circuit and overheat.
Its heat spread to the cells beside it.
Certification had assumed that wouldn't happen.
The fix added insulation between cells and a steel box around them.
The fleet returned to service months later.

baslik: A Tiny Clock Error Let a Missile Through
sonuc: failed to intercept an incoming Scud missile
tetik: a clock error growing after long continuous operation
mekanizma: time conversion rounding error accumulating over about 100 hours, shifting the tracking range gate
ders: the software was patched and operators told to reboot systems regularly
yanilgi: The missile didn't evade a working system. The system looked in the wrong place because its clock had drifted.
tartisma: A fix arrived the day after the attack. How fast should a known bug be patched?
basliklar: Why the Patriot Missile Missed at Dhahran
The Rounding Error That Drifted for 100 Hours
soru: How fast should bugs be fixed?
sahneler: A Patriot missile battery failed to stop an incoming Scud.
It hit a barracks in Dhahran, and twenty eight soldiers were killed.
The system had been running for about one hundred hours.
Its clock stored time with a tiny rounding error.
Over hours of operation, the error kept growing.
The radar looked for the Scud in the wrong place.
A software fix arrived the day after.
Operators were told to reboot the systems regularly.

baslik: Old Code on One Server Lost a Company Millions in Minutes
sonuc: lost hundreds of millions of dollars in minutes
tetik: a deployment that missed one of eight servers
mekanizma: a reused flag reactivating obsolete trading code on a server that didn't get the new software
ders: the firm was sold and US regulators tightened rules on automated trading controls
yanilgi: No hacker was involved. A manual deployment missed one server, and old code woke up.
tartisma: There was no automatic kill switch. Should every automated system have one?
basliklar: How Knight Capital Lost Millions in 45 Minutes
The Dead Code That Came Back to Life
soru: Should everything have a kill switch?
sahneler: A trading firm's computers started sending runaway stock orders.
Within minutes, the company had lost hundreds of millions of dollars.
New software had been installed the night before.
It was deployed by hand to eight servers.
One server was missed.
A reused setting woke up long-dead code on that machine.
There was no automatic kill switch.
The firm had to be rescued and sold.

baslik: Missing Engine Data Made Three Engines Freeze After Take-Off
sonuc: crashed on a test flight near Seville
tetik: engine calibration data wiped during software installation
mekanizma: missing torque calibration parameters causing engine control units to hold three engines at idle
ders: Airbus added checks that engine data is present before flight
yanilgi: The engines weren't damaged. Their control software had simply lost the data it needed to work.
tartisma: The aircraft gave no cockpit warning until airborne. When should a system refuse to start?
basliklar: Why the A400M Crashed at Seville
The Data Wiped Before a Test Flight
soru: When should a system refuse to start?
sahneler: Shortly after take-off, a new military transport crashed near Seville.
Three of its four engines froze at low power, and four crew were killed.
The engines weren't damaged.
During software installation, calibration data had been erased.
Without it, the engine controls couldn't respond.
There was no warning before take-off.
The problem appeared only once airborne.
Airbus added checks that engine data is present before flight.
